newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - seen absorbing sales easily.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - seen absorbing sales easily.

text.p: U.S. municipals in early trade on Monday were flat to slightly higher, and with an expected rise in redemptions in June and July, the market was expected to easily absorb another big week of new issues.
"I don't think there's going to be any problem cutting through supply," a trader said.
Municipal bond sales for this week were expected to total $4.3 billion in 160 deals, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Negotiated offerings added up to $3.2 billion in 73 sales, the largest total this year, with a $275 million Detroit Sewer Authority, Mich., deal through PaineWebber Inc. topping the list. Traders said that they expected the offering to be priced attractively as the underlying credit is not outstanding, though the bonds likely would be insured.
"They're going to come cheap to the market," one said.
On the competitive side, 87 sales totaling $1.1 billion were scheduled. A $200 million Massachusettes Bay Transportation Authority deal on Wednesday was the largest.
An over $150 million negotiated sale by Tampa Sports Authority also was expected to attract a fair amount of interest, in part because Florida paper often is in demand.
In light, early morning trade, a trader said that the few deals that were done changed hands at the offered side, and in the near-term, there appeared to be few clouds on the horizon.

The next economic report that has the potential to drive markets, the Consumer Price Index, was not due out until Tuesday morning. The May report was forecast at up 0.02 percent, according to a Reuters consensus survey of economists.

Traders looked for the inflation data to prove moderate, in part because last week's Producer Price Index fell in May, shedding 0.3 percent. "If the PPI was positive, I can't remember anytime the CPI wasn't," a trader said.
Secondary market supplies firmed slightly, with a closely watched yardstick, the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, climbing back above the $1 billion level to almost $1.1 billion.
Actively quoted issues included Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.48 percent, NET, unchanged.
And Jefferson County, Alabama, Sewer Revenues of 2027, which carry a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 101-1/4, unchanged.
September municipal futures rose three ticks to 111-30/32, while September Treasury futures firmed four ticks to 117-30/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 192 ticks.
